dimensions.title: Completeness
dimensions.question: Does the plan address the problems this chart actually presents?
dimensions.source: self-authored; the chart-vs-plan comparison the design calls for in §9

anchors.1: The plan addresses none of the chart's significant problems, or addresses something the chart does not record.
anchors.3: The dominant problem is addressed; one or more significant problems are absent without explanation.
anchors.5: Every significant problem in the chart is addressed by at least one concern, or its omission is defensible from the chart.

dimensions.title: Traceability
dimensions.question: Does every element trace to evidence a reader can check, and is the citation the right one?
dimensions.source: self-authored; design §8's graph invariant, judged for quality rather than presence

anchors.1: Elements cite nothing, or cite material that does not support them.
anchors.3: Every element cites something, but at least one citation is only loosely related to the claim it supports.
anchors.5: Every element cites material that genuinely supports it, and a reader following the citation would agree.

dimensions.title: Guideline concordance
dimensions.question: Is what the plan proposes consistent with the guidance it cites?
dimensions.source: self-authored; the med_safety corpus is the standard being compared against

anchors.1: The plan proposes something the cited guidance advises against.
anchors.3: The plan is broadly consistent with the guidance but adds recommendations the citations do not support.
anchors.5: Every recommendation follows from the cited guidance applied to this patient.

dimensions.title: Safety
dimensions.question: Does the plan answer the risks that were flagged, and avoid creating new ones?
dimensions.source: self-authored; the stratify rules are the risks being checked against

anchors.1: The plan proposes something contraindicated for this patient, or ignores a flag that carries immediate risk.
anchors.3: The flags are acknowledged but at least one is answered only weakly.
anchors.5: Every flag is answered by a concrete intervention, and nothing proposed introduces a new hazard.

dimensions.title: Goal quality
dimensions.question: Are the goals specific, measurable, and expressed as outcomes for the patient?
dimensions.source: self-authored; design §7 node 4 requires an outcome, not a clinician action

anchors.1: Goals restate the problem, or describe what the clinician will do rather than what changes for the patient.
anchors.3: Goals are patient-centred but vague — no target, or no timeframe.
anchors.5: Each goal names an outcome for the patient with something measurable attached.

dimensions.title: Feasibility and burden
dimensions.question: Could this patient actually carry out this plan?
dimensions.source: self-authored; the burden count from design §7 node 6

anchors.1: The plan asks more of the patient than anyone could sustain, or asks for something their circumstances rule out.
anchors.3: The plan is achievable but heavy, with several items that could be combined or sequenced.
anchors.5: The plan asks a realistic amount of a patient in these circumstances, and says who is responsible for each part.
